- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67) or volatile (alternating ±0.67), model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward by 1–4% for next 3–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion zones (e.g., 65–70 range) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 2–5% buffer for 7–14 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “1.00” extremes, model tends to misread sentiment direction; use sentiment-weighted average to anchor forecast mid-point.
